- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a price spike (forecast > true), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high for 2–4 day horizons.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–3% for next 3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates by 1–3% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day for 2–5 days after sentiment shift.
